_comment: THREAT ACTOR scoring model for scripts/osint/exposure_score.py (--model actor), documented in analysis/weight-engine.md §9. Adapted from the Threat Actor Scoring Model in [PK Packt ACTIH companion repo, 2026, chapter-01/Threat Actor Scoring Model.md] (MIT). ANALYST-RATED, never automatic: intent, capability, sectoral_reach and org_exposure are each set by the analyst on a 0.0-1.0 scale in fixed steps. The Threat Score is an analyst judgement for ONE organisation and a lead, never attribution and never a same-operator edge. Vocabulary and thresholds only, never case data (RULE 1).

settings._comment: step: the only legal rating increments (0.0, 0.25, ... 1.0). decimals: rounding of opportunity and threat_score (half-up); the band is read from the ROUNDED published score so a reader can re-derive it. floor_value: an intent rating equal to this forces the Threat Score to 0 (the Intent floor rule). evidence_required_intent: intent at or above this must cite evidence matching evidence_pattern (a URL or a case reference). drift_warn_shift: a re-score that moves the Threat Score by MORE than this without a written reason is warned (upstream score-stability guidance: most actors move no more than 0.10 a quarter).

weights._comment: Threat Score = intent x 0.5 + capability x 0.25 + opportunity x 0.25 (weights sum to 1.0). Intent carries half because a capable actor with no interest in the organisation is not a threat to it.

opportunity_weights._comment: Opportunity = sectoral_reach x 0.6 + org_exposure x 0.4. Reach is the steadier signal (it moves when the actor's behaviour moves); org_exposure moves with our own environment and is partly in our control.

dimensions._comment: id -> {name, question, scale}. All four are required for a score. The scale anchors are rephrased guidance for the 0.25 steps, printed by --list and mirrored in analysis/weight-engine.md §9.

intent.name: Intent
intent.question: does the actor want to hit this organisation, its sector or its geography?

scale.0.0: no observable interest in the sector, geography or kind of organisation
scale.0.25: only indirect signs; observed targeting sits next to us but not on us
scale.0.5: has gone after our sector or geography before, but sporadically or not lately
scale.0.75: steady, recent targeting of our sector and geography
scale.1.0: has targeted us, or openly targets organisations directly comparable to us, with recent confirmed activity

capability.name: Capability
capability.question: could the actor carry out an operation against us if it chose to?

scale.0.0: no shown offensive ability; reconsider whether the actor should be tracked at all
scale.0.25: off-the-shelf tools, weak operational discipline, opportunistic
scale.0.5: competent: some bespoke tooling, settled habits, unremarkable tradecraft
scale.0.75: bespoke tooling, disciplined tradecraft, sustained tempo, success against hardened targets
scale.1.0: top tier: unpatched-vulnerability access, low-level implants, multi-year operations against high-value targets

sectoral_reach.name: Opportunity: sectoral reach
sectoral_reach.question: does the actor operate against organisations like ours, in general?

scale.0.0: no meaningful reach to organisations like ours
scale.0.25: works in neighbouring sectors or regions only
scale.0.5: has hit organisations adjacent to our sector or in our region, not direct peers
scale.0.75: has hit direct peers, competitors or organisations on a similar technology stack
scale.1.0: recently hit direct peers and has shown access to the same kinds of systems we run

org_exposure.name: Opportunity: organisational exposure
org_exposure.question: given our current environment, can the actor actually reach us?

scale.0.0: none of the actor's known techniques apply to us and our detection covers its tradecraft
scale.0.25: little technical overlap, strong compensating controls, good detection
scale.0.5: real technical overlap with partial controls and partial visibility
scale.0.75: wide technical overlap, material control gaps, thin detection against its techniques
scale.1.0: our estate matches its tooling, controls have significant gaps, and we are blind to its techniques

bands._comment: Band -> {min (inclusive lower bound on the rounded Threat Score), review_cadence, review_cadence_days (null = no fixed cadence; reviewed only on an out-of-cycle trigger), posture[]}. Evaluated highest min first. Posture is the standing work the team keeps up against the actor, rephrased from upstream.

posture: keep a dedicated profile and re-rate every dimension monthly
run standing hunts against the actor's techniques, not one-off sweeps
test detection coverage against the actor's known tooling on a schedule
keep sharing-group and peer engagement focused on the actor
send any fresh reporting on the actor straight to intake
brief security leadership on the actor at least quarterly
re-rate each dimension at the quarterly review
hunt against the actor's techniques periodically
fold the actor's tooling into routine detection-engineering planning
route new reporting to intake at normal priority
include the actor in the yearly top-threat briefing
review the profile quarterly
cover the actor's techniques through ordinary detection work, with no dedicated stream
route new reporting to intake at standard priority
hunt only opportunistically
keep the profile, reviewed only when an out-of-cycle trigger fires
read new reporting at intake; it normally ends as a tracking note
rely on general controls; no dedicated detection or hunting
catalogue only, with the written rationale stored beside the score
the rationale is the deliverable: a later analyst must see why the actor sits this low, above all when the Intent floor rule set it
no active work; re-score only on a material change

axis1_map._comment: Actor band -> Severity Tier Matrix Axis 1 (threat severity), see severity_tiers.json. Negligible has no Axis 1 row and maps to Low with a note: the grid never closes an item, so the floor is P4 (tracked).

review_triggers._comment: Out-of-cycle re-score triggers, rephrased from upstream. Any of these re-opens the actor whatever its cadence.
values: new attribution work or a significant intelligence update on the actor
the actor is named in a peer incident relevant to our sector
a geopolitical shift between the actor's sponsor and our country
a major change on our side: acquisition, divestiture, new platform
